Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testNan()` fails because it asserts that comparing NaN > NaN should return FALSE. However, the test result reveals that the comparison `"$nan > $nan"` evaluates to TRUE, which is incorrect according to IEEE floating-point standards where NaN comparisons always return false.

Examining the test code `testNan()`, the assertion is `assertXPathValue(context, "$nan > $nan", Boolean.FALSE, Boolean.class);`, which expects the expression to evaluate as false.

Looking into the code related to the greater than operation, the `CoreOperationGreaterThan.evaluateCompare(int)` method returns `compare > 0` where `compare` is the result of some comparison between values. There is no special handling for NaN values in this code.

No signs are seen of any logic to detect NaN inputs and override the comparison result to false, which is the correct behavior mathematically.

Thus, the bug is that the comparison logic in `CoreOperationGreaterThan` (or its related comparison mechanisms) fails to correctly handle NaN values, causing `NaN > NaN` to incorrectly evaluate to true.

No relevant information is found in recent bug reports, so the diagnosis is based solely on the current test and code snippets.

This defect can be fixed by introducing explicit handling for NaN cases in the comparison logic to ensure any comparison involving NaN returns false, which is the expected and mathematically correct behavior.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
